attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm part is that infrastructure spending 'enormously outweighed' total revenue. The $250B and 50:1 figures are hedged with 'perhaps', and the drafter keeps that qualifier.

contract.note: Scoring only the firm qualitative comparison is a fair, ordinary reading, and treating the numbers as tentative is fair. Because the start date, industry boundaries and accounting basis are unspecified, any result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Sequoia's 2023–24 estimate of the annual revenue needed to justify the spending. It does not compare realized cumulative spending with realized revenue.
IDC's estimate of 2024 AI infrastructure spending ($153B), available before the evaluation date. It gives one year of spending only and no matching revenue figure.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives an annual infrastructure spending figure and a Sequoia estimate of the revenue needed, but no matching realized revenue series for the same industry and period. Spending far ahead of revenue is plausible, but the evidence here does not establish or refute the cumulative comparison.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: An unhedged 'will' with the antecedent kept. 'Offsetting' is loose wording: Marcus does not say losses exceed construction jobs, and the contract corrects this. 'Net effect is entirely unclear' expresses uncertainty, not a separate forecast.

contract.note: Not requiring a negative net effect is fair. The meaning of 'better AI' and the threshold for 'many' are interpretations the contract supplies, not the speaker.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that parts of the Abilene site run early training workloads. It does not show a capability improvement attributable to the facility, so the antecedent is not established.
The developer reports construction jobs at the site, which bears only on the 'some people will be employed' aside. It says nothing about the conditional consequent of job losses.
Yale Budget Lab finds no broad link between AI exposure and employment so far. It does not isolate Stargate and does not rule out later displacement.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, that the data centers produce better AI, is not established in the packet, and no deadline was stated. A conditional with an unknown antecedent is not scored, and no conclusive event documents displacement attributable to these facilities. Construction employment covers only the aside.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: A passing present-tense remark in a list of objections. 'Immense' is an evaluative adjective with no measure, scope or timeframe, so it works as rhetoric rather than a testable observation or forecast.

contract.note: The contract turns a present-tense remark into a forecast about realized Stargate environmental impacts. Marcus supplied neither that forward-looking reading nor the project boundaries, and the contract also conflicts with the drafter's 'observation' kind.

evidence.note: News report on the Abilene site's scale and its 360 MW gas plant. This shows capacity and permits, not realized environmental impacts.
OpenAI's own claims about reducing water use. This is design intent, not a measured lifecycle impact.

reviews.rationale: 'Immense environmental cost' is a rhetorical aside with no measure, scope or horizon, so it cannot be scored. Even under the contract's forecast reading, the packet has only capacity, permits and developer claims, with no realized impact data.
